notes.claim: A transformer's turns ratio is the same as its voltage ratio, so a 10 : 1 transformer steps voltage in the ratio 10 : 1.
The order of the numbers in a transformer's turns ratio is very important.
A compression ratio of six means the mixture is compressed to one-sixth of its original volume, so it is a ratio of two volumes.
In one study of ratio sharing, confusion about the whole was the misconception that appeared most often, and NCTM advises teaching part-to-part against part-to-whole ratios explicitly.
A marine gearbox's reduction ratio is usually between 2 : 1 and 3 : 1 on small marine diesels (a magazine's figure, not a standard).

sources.title: Transformer Basics and Transformer Principles, Electronics Tutorials
sources.quote: the turns ratio of any given transformer will be the same as its voltage ratio.

sources.title: Transformer Basics and Transformer Principles, Electronics Tutorials
sources.quote: Note that the order of the numbers when expressing a transformers turns ratio value is very important

sources.title: Step-up and Step-down Transformers, All About Circuits
sources.quote: Turns ratio of 10:1 yields 10:1 primary:secondary voltage ratio and 1:10 primary:secondary current ratio.

sources.title: How it works: Marine gearboxes and clutches, Yachting Monthly
sources.quote: The reduction gear ratio is usually between 2:1 and 3:1, with different manufacturers often using differing ratios.

sources.title: Compression ratio, Britannica
sources.quote: A compression ratio of six means that the mixture is compressed to one-sixth its original volume by the action of the piston in the cylinder.

sources.title: Compression ratio, Britannica
sources.quote: It is defined as the maximum volume of the combustion chamber (with the piston farthest out, or bottom dead centre) divided by the volume with the piston in the full-compression position

sources.title: Misconceptions on part-part-whole proportional relationships, Taylor & Francis
sources.quote: Confusion about the whole was the misconception that appeared most frequently across all grades.

sources.title: Ratios and Proportional Relationships, NCTM
sources.quote: Ask students to explain part-to-part versus part-to-whole ratios.
